_comment: Spatial words drawn as a picture, not searched for and not clozed (tunatale-hvj0, the user 2026-09-28: 'they become picture cards'). Each maps a word to a language-neutral concept in app.cards.spatial_scenes.SPATIAL_CONCEPTS. A word listed here is NOT a function word, whatever `function_words.json` or a POS tag says: app.srs.function_words.is_function_word vetoes it, so it cards as vocab and its image is drawn. The picture is only drawn when the card's English gloss names the relation (app.cards.spatial_picture.gloss_matches), which is what keeps a homograph's other sense off the picture. Map only words whose MAIN sense is spatial: the case marker 'sa' stays a cloze. 'wala' (none / left), 'tuo' (right / believe) and 'tunga' (half / middle) are homographs: they are listed, and the gloss guard draws them only on a card glossed with the spatial sense. ORCHESTRATOR-DRAFTED, not native-checked. Distinct words get distinct pictures (2026-09-29, tunatale-fsyd): kilid ('side') no longer shares tupad's beside, and tunga ('middle') no longer shares taliwala's between; both are parts of the box, like top and bottom. 2026-10-14: gikan (from) and padulong (toward) added, drawn with a flag for the place; the user chose the flag over a house. 2026-10-14 (tunatale-qas4): the four distances from the people talking, after Wolff: kini 'this (near speaker and person spoken to)', kiri 'near speaker but not near hearer', kana 'near hearer', kadto 'far from speaker and hearer', and dinhi / diri / diha / didto for places. Wolff has no diri headword; it follows ari ('here, near speaker but not near person spoken to') the way dinhi follows anhi. The user kept all four distances.
